subject: Need to edit a string in methylDiff object

messages.author: acaba9010f6f5153
messages.subject: Need to edit a string in methylDiff object
parts:
Hello,
I'm trying to align the DMRs against the gene parts annotations - generated from a bed file. I am having issues with the annotateWithGeneParts command -  I think this is due to different chromosome naming conventions between the gene model file & the coverage file generated from BS-seq data. 
I attempted modifying the chromosome names in the bedfile, but that didn't work. I want to try edit the name in the chromosome field in my DMR table - produced in methylKit with the getMethylDiff command - I've attempted this using str_replace - this doesn't work. I get the following error from the code:

DMRS <- myDiff25p %>% mutate(chr = str_replace(chr, 'M821.3ch*', 'chr'))

Error in `vec_data()`:
! `x` must be a vector, not a <methylDiff> object.

So I believe I need to convert this object to a vector but I'm having difficulties. If anyone can help, it'd be very appreciated! 
Thanks, Caleb

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: Need to edit a string in methylDiff object
parts:
Hi Caleb,

The difference in chromosome naming conventions is a common problem in bioinformatics, that you are going to encounter many more times in the future ;)
My recommendation would be to either fetch a matching annotation or learn how to modify annotation files to adjust the chromosome naming yourself using the sed command. This way you fix the annotation in the beginning and make sure it matches with any downstream output. 

Anyways, back to your problem. 

The dplyr functions are expecting a `data.frame` to do their job and while a methylDiff is derived from a data.frame it is not directly supported. 

If you want to use tidyverse functions on methylKit objects I suggest you first convert the objects to data.frame using `getData`:
```myDiff25p %>% getData %>%  mutate(chr = str_replace(chr, 'M821.3ch*', 'chr'))```

However, since a methylDiff is derived from a data.frame you may also just directly change the chromosome column:
```myDiff25p$chr <- str_replace(myDiff25p$chr, 'M821.3ch*', 'chr')```


Best,
Alex
